# Breen-Deligne　`thm.breen-deligne`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=thm.breen-deligne)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./thm.breen-deligne.md)

## Notes · **draft**
**What it says.** In a general topos "free object" is not finite (the $s$ in $M^{s}$ is a **set** and may have arbitrarily large cardinality). The theorem says that nevertheless any abelian group $M$ can be resolved by a **termwise free** complex, and the resolution is **natural** (independent of choices, functorial in $M$).

**What $\mathbb{Z} \cdot X$ is**: the **free abelian group** generated by the set $X$ (in a topos, $\mathbb{Z}[X]$). $M^{s}$ is "the product of $s$ copies of $M$" — the power set is taken so that "elements of $M$" can be written as a countable combination.
